endorsements.quote: This implementation needs to go hand-in-hand with education of citizens/patients and health professionals.

The involvement of dermatologists in the development of these digital technologies, together with other disciplines such as anthropologists or sociologists should be also considered to help associate them with human perspectives and values, while ensuring good acceptance when launched.
Therefore, prospective studies including large cohorts with different populations and ethnicities in clinical practice are urgently needed to validate them [30,31].
Adequate pre- and post-marketing certification is also required.

unlisted_practices: Promote EU policies to decrease inequalities in skin cancer care among different populations and countries.
Define data protection policies and guidelines for consumers, companies, and health professionals guiding the implementation of AI skin cancer technologies.
Developers should support trustworthy third-party access to data and code within technical feasibility while respecting intellectual property.
Stakeholders including society, health policy makers, companies, clinicians, and patients should agree on post-marketing quality assurance for AI digital health solutions.
AI skin cancer applications should report model performance with good quality standard metrics, model confidence calibration, and model interpretability.
Implement digital health education in the medical curriculum.
Keep dermatologists involved in e-health policy-making to ensure systems are effective, reliable, safe, and ethical.
Ensure strict evaluation and EU certification of skin cancer AI applications.

screen.reason: Multidisciplinary expert consensus statement discussing challenges in skin cancer management and implementation of digital health and AI technologies.
